title: Recover complementary PWM with dead-time insertion
description: Reverse engineer a gate-level netlist and an obfuscated RTL wrapper describing a 4-bit-programmable complementary PWM generator with a fixed 16-clock period, used to drive a two-switch half-bridge gate driver. Submit a clean, word-level Verilog module that reproduces the exact same cycle-accurate behavior, including the safety gap inserted around every duty-cycle transition.

expected_output.notes: Must be a single self-contained file, compilable standalone with iverilog, matching the pinned port list exactly.

metrics.name: cycle_accurate_match_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of simulated clock cycles across all test vectors (duty sweep 0-15, reset sequences, enable-hold sequences) where submission pwm_hi and pwm_lo exactly match the independently generated reference design's outputs.

metrics.name: overlap_violation_count
metrics.description: Number of clock cycles observed during simulation where pwm_hi and pwm_lo are simultaneously high; must be zero for the submission to pass regardless of other scores.

metrics.name: deadtime_width_error
metrics.description: Sum of absolute differences between the observed dead-time gap length (in cycles) and the required 2-cycle gap, measured at both period-start and duty-boundary transitions across all tested duty values.

metrics.name: functional_equivalence
metrics.description: Boolean pass/fail indicating whether the recovered RTL, when compiled and simulated, is behaviorally equivalent (bit-exact, cycle-exact) to the reference across the full FR1-FR4 and SR1-SR2 test suite.

submission_contract.note: Participants do not edit files under inputs/. They replace the placeholder at submission/recovered_rtl.v with their recovered design. The shipped starting file is a naive placeholder and is expected to fail evaluation.
